implementation: Closed author-owned canonical-v1 constant; same sole business input projectDirectory. No source/clock/provider/env URL overrides or implicit source fallback.

Complete canonical install-v1 packument, not slim version inference: validates identity, version keys, modified time, dist-tag references, exact installed/latest manifest engines/peers/dist and SemVer series.
Only nineteen named supported public tools, now including Vite, may be queried. Unknown/private names and URLs are rejected before fetch.
Mutable facts require valid HTTP Date/Age <=1h with stale/error states rejected. Conflicting body modified time is unconfirmed. Errors never fall back to cached success, mirror or npmx.

Node exact-release existence and LTS-at-release come only from the official historical index; actual old index cache age is explicitly recorded. Current lifecycle observation time comes only from the fresh official GitHub contents schedule. Missing exact historical release is unconfirmed.

Legitimate official Node prerelease history entries such as v27.0.0-alpha.0.1.0 are validated and retained without rejecting unrelated supported stable LTS records. Selecting a prerelease default remains mismatch; malformed historical records remain unconfirmed.

Required and optional peers resolve from the selected tool's exact owning importer reference and v9 snapshot, follow dependencies/optionalDependencies or consistent peer suffix, and require the exact peer snapshot and packages integrity record. Other importers and globally matching snapshots never substitute. Vite does not need an unused direct devDependency; its selected version's range and Node engine compatibility are checked.

Scripts retains one statically parsed Turbo scheduler invocation per responsible project directory while expanding member tasks. Convention includes these scheduler commands when determining required directly used dev tooling; normal declaration, exact importer, freshness and Node checks apply. No shell keyword scan or separate policy mechanism.
Official GitHub schedule contents validate path/type/base64/size/Git blob SHA plus lifecycle schema. Current supported LTS versus EOL uses that fresh schedule.

Bounds: 10s/request, 90s/execution, 16MiB/response, 128MiB/execution, 66 requests, 64 package cache entries, 32768 versions/packument, 20000 historical Node records, 256KiB schedule, 256 lifecycle series.
Fixed original eleven lint failures using actual narrowing, without suppression.
Preserved Files guards/read budgets, fixed AGENTS assets, publisher positive support, static-only target inspection, SDK ownership and strict input.

major >=1, 0.minor patch-only, exact 0.0.patch and scoped package paths

stale/invalid HTTP cache metadata, wrong media type, malformed/modified-after-response metadata, network failures, cancellation and unexpected faults
